linkedin:
Nvidia’s newest RTX Spark laptops promise desktop‑class AI performance, but a hidden Windows‑only power controller is throttling Linux workloads, according to the recent blog.

On a 120‑billion‑parameter model, native Linux delivers only 13.9 tokens per second, roughly 35 % of the 65 tokens per second seen on Windows. The GPU clock collapses from over 2 GHz on Windows to about 780 MHz on Linux when plugged in.

The root cause is an encrypted firmware power table that only the Windows driver can decrypt. Linux lacks this logic, so it falls back to a safe, low‑power clock. Using WSL 2, which runs on the Windows driver stack, restores the full boost and yields 65.1 tokens per second, essentially identical to native Windows.

"The encrypted power‑table is the missing piece for Linux performance."  

This matters because developers expecting laptop‑scale AI throughput are forced to stay on Windows or use WSL, undermining the portability promise of the Spark line.

The data reflects current driver and firmware behavior; future Nvidia updates could change the picture.

Will you adopt WSL for your AI workloads on RTX Spark, or wait for a Linux driver fix?  

Full breakdown with sources: https://buildwithsaksham.in/blog/nvidia-rtx-spark-encrypted-firmware-slows-inference-speed-by
